title: Haplotypes: V K O R C one and T P M T star three A

segs.text: Section three. Haplotype nomenclature. A haplotype is a set of variants at several loci on one allele that occur together in the population more often than random chance. When the same combination of changes keeps turning up in different people, it is common enough to be worth one name, and one name is easier to say and read than the list of changes. Whoever discovers a haplotype names it, so the naming differs from gene to gene.

V K O R C one has at least ten S N Ps that may have a functional effect, and they group together in different ways. She said, There's one called haplotype A, and there's another called haplotype B. Haplotype B is the most common. These haplotypes matter for their functional significance, and V K O R C one comes back later as the gene she pairs with warfarin dosing.

T P M T, thiopurine methyltransferase, uses a star name with a letter instead. The allele was first called T P M T star three. She said, We did some more work and realized that three is actually two snips in the gene. So it was renamed star three A. The two changes on one allele are six fifteen, G to A, and eight seventy four, A to G. Together they give significantly reduced T P M T activity, which matters for azathioprine and six mercaptopurine.

A haplotype is several variants together on one allele, while a genotype is the two alleles a person carries. Not every gene's haplotypes are lettered. Naming is up to the discoverers, and some get star names, like T P M T star three A. V K O R C one is the gene she pairs with warfarin, and T P M T goes with azathioprine and six mercaptopurine.
